plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Rolling Provençal hillsides turn into rippling waves of violet-blue, with a sweet, herbal perfume that drifts on the warm summer air and draws clouds of buzzing bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to early August, with peak color in mid-July
plants.funFact: Lavender's name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Drooping rosy-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. Bees and butterflies crowd these tough prairie natives all summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to September, sometimes reblooming in fall
plants.location: Eastern and central North American prairies and gardens
plants.funFact: The spiky center is actually a dense cluster of tiny disc flowers. The seed heads feed goldfinches into autumn.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest flower head in the protea family is a bowl of silky, pink-tipped bracts around a thistle-like center. It blooms in the cool of the Southern Hemisphere winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Roughly April to October, depending on the local climate
plants.location: Fynbos shrublands of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. It is adapted to fire-prone fynbos, and its thick underground stems can resprout after a blaze.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Huge, glowing blooms rise on tall stalks above round, water-beading leaves. Each flower opens at dawn and closes at dusk, and can span about a foot.
plants.location: Ponds and wetlands across Asia, including China and Japan
plants.funFact: Each flower lasts only about three days. The leaf surface repels water so well that it inspired the term 'lotus effect' in self-cleaning materials.
